verses.1: And it happened on the day that Moses began to build the Tabernacle. He sanctified it and all its utensils, as well as the altar and all its utensils. He made them holy.
verses.2: And the leaders of Israel, the heads of their families, they were those who held positions of authority. They stood at the forefront of those in power.
verses.3: And they brought their offerings before Jehovah: six golden calves, and twelve bronze calves. They also offered two oxen, one for each of the priests who carried the offerings. They presented these offerings before the altar.
verses.4: And the LORD said to Moses, “Say…”
verses.5: Take them and make them serve in the service of the Tabernacle. Then you will give them to the Levites, one person for each person who serves.
verses.6: And Moses took the wheels and the poles, and he gave them to the Levites.
verses.7: The two wheels and the four oxen were given to the sons of Gershon as payment for their labor.
verses.8: And the four wheels and the position of the morning sun were given to the sons of Merari, as a reward for their work, by Itamar, son of Aaron, the priest.
verses.9: And the doors of Khetah were not given to them, as it is said that the service of the Holy One should be carried out on their shoulders.
verses.10: And the priests brought the offerings to the altar on the day they sacrificed him. And the priests also brought their offerings before the altar.
verses.11: And the LORD said to Moses, “On one day, there will be a day when they will offer their sacrifices to the Lord. They will bring their offerings before the altar.”
verses.12: And on that first day, Nahshon son of Aminadab presented his offering to the altar of Jehovah.
verses.13: And we brought one basket of silver, weighing one hundred and thirty pounds. Each pound was worth seventy shekels. Both baskets were filled with fragrant spices in their containers for use as an offering.
verses.14: One hand, filled with twelve pieces of gold.
verses.15: One son from the morning; one son from the evening. One son from his year of birth, to rise up.
verses.16: One hair of the beard is enough for one person’s punishment.
verses.17: And for the sacrifice of sacrifices, two sheep, five lambs, five doves, and five year-old goats. This is the sacrifice that Nakhshon son of Imindab offered.
verses.18: On the second day, Nataniel, son of Zua’ar, became the king of Isashkhar.
verses.19: Bring forward one silver coin, weighing thirty and one hundred grams. This coin is worth seventy shekels. Both coins should be filled with honey as an offering.
verses.20: One hand, twelve gold rings filled with gold.
verses.21: One son from the morning, one son from the evening; one son from his year of birth.
verses.22: One strong hair for one’s hair.
verses.23: And for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two sheep, five lambs, five heifers, and five year-old goats. This is the sacrifice that Nathaniel son of Zuar offered.
verses.24: On the third day, Eliezer son of Jalon became the ruler of Zebulun.
verses.25: We brought along one bag of silver, weighing three hundred and ten pounds. Each bag contained seventy shекелs of silver. Both bags were filled with fine flour, used as an offering.
verses.26: One hand, twelve golden rings filled with gold.
verses.27: One son from the morning, one son from the evening; one son from his year of birth, to rise up.
verses.29: And for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two sheep, five lambs, five heifers, and five year-old calves. This is the sacrifice offered by Eliyahu son of Chelon.
verses.30: On the fourth day, Reuben’s son, Elizur, son of Shedeur, became king.
verses.31: We prepared one jar containing thirty-one hundred pounds. Each jar weighed seventy shекелs. Both jars were filled with honey as an offering.
verses.32: One hand is filled with twelve pieces of gold.
verses.33: One son from the morning; one son from the evening. One son from his year of birth, to go up.
verses.34: One hair of the beard for punishment.
verses.35: And for the sacrifice of the sacrifices, two lambs, five rams, five heifers, and five goats. This is the sacrifice offered to Elišur, son of Shadiyur.
verses.36: On the fifth day, Zulmiyel son of Surishadai became the ruler of Benjamin.
verses.37: We brought along one bag of silver, weighing three hundred and ten pounds. Each bag contained seventy shекלs of silver. Both bags were filled with pure gold for use as offerings.
verses.38: One hand, twelve gold pieces filled with gold.
verses.39: One son from the morning; one son from the evening. One son from his year of birth, to go up.
verses.40: One young goat for the sacrifice
verses.41: And for the sacrifice of sacrifices, two sheep, five lambs, five bulls, five rams, and five heifers. This is the sacrifice offered by Samuel son of Saul.
verses.42: On the fifth day of the month, Nathaniel went to Eliyahu’s son, Eliezer.
verses.43: We brought along one jar of silver, weighing three hundred and ten pounds. Each jar contained seventy shекלs of silver. Both jars were filled with pure honey for use as an offering.
verses.44: One hand, filled with twelve pieces of gold.
verses.45: One child from the morning; one child from the evening. One child from his year, to go up.
verses.46: One wild dog for one offense.
verses.47: And for the sacrifice of holiness, two lambs, five rams, five goats, and five young male lambs were offered. This was a sacrifice to Eleazar son of Dodai.
verses.48: On the seventh day, Elishama son of Abiud became king over the people of Ephraim.
verses.49: We brought along one bag of silver, weighing three hundred and ten pounds. Each bag contained seventy pounds of silver. Both bags were filled with fine spices for use as offerings.
verses.50: One hand, twelve pieces of gold, filled with precious stones.
verses.51: One child from the morning; one child from the evening. One child from his year of birth, to rise up.
verses.52: One hair of the head is enough for punishment.
verses.53: And for the sacrifice of sacrifices, two lambs, five rams, five heifers, and five young goats. This is the sacrifice that Eliezer son of Jemiah offered.
verses.54: On the eighth day, Menashe’s son, Gamliel, son of Peda-Tzur, became king.
verses.55: We brought along one bag of silver, weighing three hundred and ten pounds. Each bag contained seventy shекелs of silver. Both bags were filled with fine flour in the form of offerings.
verses.56: One hand, twelve gold rings filled with gold.
verses.57: One child from the morning, one child from the evening; one child from his year, to go up.
verses.58: One young goat for the sacrifice.
verses.59: And for the sacrifice of sacrifices, two lambs, five yearlings, five rams, and five heifers. This is the ritual offering of Gamliel son of Peda Zur.
verses.60: On the ninth day, Rehobam ben Benyamin became king. Abidan ben Gideon was his father.
verses.61: We brought along one bag of silver, weighing three hundred and ten pounds. Each bag contained seventy pounds of silver. Both bags were filled with fine spices for use as offerings.
verses.62: One hand, filled with twelve pieces of gold.
verses.63: One son from the morning; one son from the evening. One son from his year of birth, to go up.
verses.64: One hair of the beard is enough for punishment.
verses.65: And for the sacrifice of holiness, two sheep, five lambs, five heifers, and five year-old lambs were used. This was the sacrifice that Abidan son of Gidon offered.
verses.66: On the fiftieth day, Ahijzer, son of Ismael, became the ruler of the people of Dan.
verses.67: We brought along one jar of silver, weighing three hundred and ten pounds. Each jar contained seventy shекелs of silver. Both jars were filled with pure honey as an offering.
verses.68: One hand, twelve gold pieces filled with gold
verses.69: One son from the morning; one son from the evening. One son from his year, up.
verses.70: One strong branch for the purpose of cutting.
verses.71: And for the sacrifice of holiness, two sheep, five lambs, five calves, and five doves. This is the offering that Ahizreel, son of Imshadai, offered.
verses.72: On the twelfth day after Abishai son of Ahron died.
verses.73: We brought along one bag of silver, weighing three hundred and ten pounds. Each bag contained seventy shекелs of silver. Both bags were filled with fine spices for use as incense.
verses.74: One hand, twelve golden rings filled with gold.
verses.75: One son from the morning; one son from the evening. One son from his year of birth, to go up.
verses.76: One hair of the beard for punishment.
verses.77: And for the sacrifice of offerings, two sheep, five lambs, five heifers, and five year-old calves. This is the sacrifice that Phaggai son of Ochran offered.
verses.78: On the twenty-second day after his reign, Ben-Naphtali Ahir’a ben-Eynan died.
verses.79: We brought one basket of silver, weighing three hundred and ten pounds. Each basket contained seventy shекелs of silver. Both baskets were filled with fine flour, used as an offering.
verses.80: One hand, twelve pieces of gold, filled with gold.
verses.81: One son from the morning; one son from the evening. One son from his year of birth, to go up.
verses.83: And for the sacrifice of offerings, two sheep, five lambs, five goats, and five young calves were required. This was the sacrifice that Ahiraban Ben-Einan offered.
verses.84: This is the amount of money that was given as a sacrifice on the day that the Israelites sacrificed their sacrifices to God. It consisted of twelve silver bowls, twelve golden bowls, and twelve shekels of gold.
verses.85: Thirty and one hundred of those containers are worth gold. Seven hundred of those jars are also worth gold. All these items total up to several hundred and forty tons per sacred vessel.
verses.86: There are twenty-one gold plates. Each plate is filled with twelve units of gold. The total weight of all the gold plates is one hundred and twenty units.
verses.87: Every morning, two dozen sheep are slaughtered. They’re also used as food for the people of that year. In addition, two dozen goat skins are also used for various purposes.
verses.88: And all the offerings of the sacrifices were forty-four sheep and sixty rams. These were all offered as sacrifices during the festival. This was the offering that was given after the sacrifice was slaughtered.
verses.89: And when Moses entered the tabernacle to speak with God, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the curtain that was on the entrance of the tabernacle. And God spoke to him.
